note: Optional question templates for StudyTrace ESM surveys, in AWARE ESM format. Nothing here is sent to participants until a researcher adds it to a schedule and saves. Wording is short-form and intended for momentary (EMA) or daily use; confirm instruments and wording with your IRB and cite the sources listed for each template.

templates.label: Momentary affect (pleasantness + energy)
templates.source: Two-item valence/arousal ratings based on the circumplex model of affect (Russell, 1980).

questions.esm_instructions: How pleasant or unpleasant do you feel right now?
How calm or energized do you feel right now?

templates.label: Momentary stress (single item)
templates.source: Single-item momentary stress rating, as commonly used in EMA studies.

questions.esm_instructions: How stressed do you feel right now?

templates.label: Momentary loneliness (single item)
templates.source: Single-item momentary loneliness rating. For a validated trait measure, consider the 3-item loneliness scale (Hughes et al., 2004) in a daily or baseline survey.

questions.esm_instructions: Right now, how lonely do you feel?

templates.label: Self-estimated phone use (yesterday)
templates.source: Self-estimate to compare with logged use (phone_use_daily, screen_time_activity), e.g. to study self-report bias (Parry et al., 2021).

questions.esm_instructions: About how many hours in total did you spend using your phone yesterday? A best guess is fine.

templates.label: Morning sleep diary
templates.source: Items adapted from the Consensus Sleep Diary (Carney et al., 2012), plus phone use in bed. Schedule once each morning.

questions.esm_instructions: What time did you try to go to sleep last night?
About how many minutes did it take you to fall asleep?
What time was your final awakening this morning?
How would you rate the quality of your sleep last night?
Did you use your phone in bed before falling asleep last night?
